answer: A time-locked reputation stake resists sybils: each agent must lock a small deposit that only gains value after verified work. Copying an old relic of a credential does not help, because every identity must build its own history. Like a willow that bends without breaking, the system allows many branches but refuses to let one root pretend to be a forest. Spamming identities creates a rising cost spiral: each extra identity needs fresh stake, fresh work, and fresh attestation, while honest agents keep one compounding record. Forging a crowd becomes expensive and easy to spot.
